1(a).assumed: Acceleration is the gradient of a v–t graph; negative when slowing.

1(b).assumed: Distance = area under v–t graph (trapezium or rectangle plus triangle).

1(c).assumed: Real deceleration varies and builds gradually; resistive forces depend on speed, so the graph would curve.

2(a)(i).assumed: Mean diameter; sphere volume 4/3πr³; mass = density × volume.

2(a)(ii).assumed: Half-range uncertainty in d; tripled for volume; add density's percentage uncertainty.

2(b)(i).assumed: A floating object displaces its own mass of water; submerged depth = displaced volume ÷ area; subtract from height.

2(b)(ii).assumed: Sea water is denser, so less volume is displaced for the same weight and the cylinder floats higher.

3(a)(i).assumed: Conventional current is in the direction positive charge would move, opposite to negative carriers.

3(a)(ii).assumed: Ions in electrolyte move towards the oppositely charged terminal; greater distance in the same time means faster.

3(b)(ii).assumed: p.d.s in series are in the ratio of resistances.

3(b)(iii).assumed: With a fixed resistor much larger than the sensor, nearly all p.d. is across it, so output hardly changes.

4(a).assumed: Both are energy per unit charge; e.m.f. converts other energy to electrical, p.d. electrical to other forms.

4(b).assumed: Uniform wire potentiometer: p.d. ∝ length; find balance lengths with zero galvanometer current; e.m.f. ratio = length ratio.

5(a)(i).assumed: Name forces on the trolley: weight, normal contact, push, friction; balanced pairs at constant velocity.

5(a)(ii).assumed: Constant velocity means zero resultant force, so push equals friction.

5(b)(i).assumed: Power = work/time, work = force × distance, distance/time = velocity.

5(b)(ii).assumed: Height gained = distance along slope × sin θ; work = mgh.

5(b)(iii).assumed: Total force = weight component plus friction; P = Fv.

6(a).assumed: Total momentum before equals total after, provided no external force acts.

6(b)(i).assumed: Speed = card length ÷ light-gate time; p = mv.

6(b)(ii).assumed: Impulse on R equals momentum lost by L, with rebound taken as negative.

6(c).assumed: Momentum conservation gives common speed; compare KE before and after; KE loss means inelastic.

7(a).assumed: Photon energy hc/λ; photons per second = power ÷ photon energy.

7(b)(ii).assumed: Measure across many fringes with calipers and divide by the number of spacings.

7(b)(iii).assumed: Rearrange λ = ax/D for a; give 3 s.f.

7(c)(i).assumed: Wavelength in glass = wavelength in air ÷ n.

7(c)(ii).assumed: Equilateral prism geometry gives r = 30° when ray is parallel to base; sin i = n sin r.

8.assumed: Find striking p.d. reliably (shield, repeat); plot V against f; h = e × gradient; K from intercept; worst line for uncertainty.
